dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: Hello. Do the referees need my help?

dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: Ah, seems like I've got the wrong person.

dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: Yes, I'm a photographer for the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: Aside from media coverage and record-keeping, my photos are also sometimes referred to when the referees make tricky decisions.

dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: The arena can get quite chaotic, and it can sometimes be difficult to tell exactly what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: Making the right call can be challenging when all each person has to go on is what they saw, so my photos are a game-changer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What if you didn't get a picture in either?

dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: That would be the trickiest set of circumstances. Perhaps the only option would be to allow the match to run into extra time.

dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: But that kind of thing doesn't happen very often. Aside from the fact that there are many referees presiding over each match, we've also got the Pyro Archon watching every moment of the action from up high.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could I ask you to take a picture for me?

dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: No can do, I'm sorry to say.

dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: Fans have asked me before if I'd sell my photos so they could go get contestants' autographs, but I always refuse. I don't want people to start reselling them for extortionate prices.

dialogues.speaker: Yokina
dialogues.text: Plus, given that I actually have to assist the referees at times, I don't accept private commissions — all in the interest of fairness, you understand.
